scope: esk-init --check / canary truthfulness (ADR-0075): canary runs the hook's effective node+emitterRef (not process.execPath); --check drifts on a different clone (#136, case-folded) and uncommitted always-on/ edits (#135); the drift fix-command echoes the user's real invocation (#137). esk-init is not a manifest gate, so no sha/version change.

boundary.evidence: the checks live in assess()/canary(), the functions that own --check

ownership.evidence: marker.repo is the single record of which clone the hook points at; compared with the shared samePath helper

dependency.evidence: canary spawns node with an args array (no shell injection, no shell-binary dependency)

error-handling.evidence: git-state check fails open (try/catch, non-git skip); canary reports a clear why on any failure

notes: Three moderate violations found and FIXED: V1 (#136 used raw !== and re-opened the Windows drive-case false-positive the repo already solves) -> now uses samePath(resolve(marker.repo), repoRoot); V3 (#137 fix-command dropped --settings/--repo/--shell) -> now echoes the user's actual argv minus --check plus --yes; and the canary was simplified to run node+expanded-emitterRef directly, removing a powershell-on-Linux failure the first cut introduced (N2).

V2 (honest): the #138 test proves the canary runs the configured target and fails on a broken emitter, but cannot fully isolate node+emitterRef from process.execPath+raw-emitter because both resolve to the same node and file for a standard install; the behavioral change lives in the code, documented in ADR-0075.
N1 (documented): the --check tests using --repo <this repo> now couple to this repo's always-on/ cleanliness (clean in CI; a dev mid-edit would see drift, which is arguably correct).
Install path intact: 44/44 esk-init tests pass; canary runs for both forms via the node invocation.
